<thought>Based on the Peterson reaction, the target alkene can be retrosynthetically disconnected into a diaryl ketone and a trimethylsilylmethyl reagent. The ketone precursor is O=C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2 and the silyl reagent is trimethylsilylmethane, C[Si](C)(C)C. These two precursors together can generate the target alkene via the Peterson elimination.</thought>
<final_answer>[[\"O=C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2\", \"C[Si](C)(C)C\"]]</final_answer>
